https://www.dw.com/en/the-crusades-how-a.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5MKWO Crusaders sewed blood-red crosses onto their garments to symbolize their commitment to Holy War. They are depicted here in defeat after Saladin recaptured Jerusalem in 1187 Image: akg-images/picture alliance Advertisement "The present moment is much like the 11th century. ... We don't want to fight, but, like our fellow Christians a thousand years ago, we must." Those are the words of US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth in his 2020 book, "American Crusade: Our Fight to Stay Free." Hegseth has repeatedly used the biblical language and symbolism of the Crusades to frame both domestic and foreign policy, from the current war in Iran to the "fight" against the "scourge of leftism." Nearly 1,000 years have passed since the November day in 1095 when Pope Urban II delivered the fiery speech that would ignite centuries of warfare and change the course of history. But Hegseth is only the latest in a long line of politicians and extremists to reference the Crusades — from the Ku Klux Klan to US President George W. Bush and Osama bin Laden . Why do the Crusades remain such a powerful source of inspiration for contemporary leaders? Princes and peasants promised eternal salvation The history of the Crusades is long and complex. But it can be summarized as an extraordinary example of how religion can become a powerful tool for political goals, helping leaders to unite people, justify wars and mobilize support on a massive scale. In the mid-11th century, Muslim Seljuk Turks conquered vast swaths of territory in the Middle East. In the early 1070s, they took control of Jerusalem, the most important holy site in Christendom. Rumors spread that pilgrims and Christians living in the region were being persecuted, and holy sites desecrated. At the Council of Clermont in 1095, Pope Urban II used the words that would become the battle cry of the Crusaders: 'Deus vult!' ('God wills it!') Image: Fine Art Images/Heritage Images/IMAGO The papacy in Rome at the time was locked in a bitter power struggle with Holy Roman Emperor Henry IV over who really held the reins of power in Western Christendom. When Byzantine Emperor Alexios I Komnenos appealed to Pope Urban II for help to defend against the Seljuks in 1095, it presented the papacy with an opportunity to demonstrate its power by bypassing Henry to rally Europe's nobility for nothing less than Holy War. Urban believed that a major Christian cause would strengthen his authority by uniting Western Europe toward a common external enemy. War was the status quo in medieval Europe, which had been hit by a series of droughts, famines and plagues. Belief in the "end times" was widespread. In this context, Urban's call for a Holy War to "liberate the Church of God" was persuasive: He demonized Muslims and promised Crusaders complete forgiveness for all past sins — as well as eternal salvation. "If you think about what a Crusade is, it's asking people to go into the unknown, thousands of miles into an unknown land," said Jonathan Phillips, an expert on crusading history at Royal Holloway University in London. Their chances of dying were about 35% to 40%, he said. So they had "to be driven by something. Religion has to come at the top," he added. Crusaders murdered thousands of Jews, whom they believed to be "enemies of Christ," during the Rhineland Massacres in 1096 Image: Fine Art Images/Heritage Images/IMAGO Urban's call to Holy War was taken up by men and women from every level of society, from "princes to peasants," Phillips said. A "tabby cat army," as he describes it, composed of peasants, low-ranking knights and nobles, and led by preachers, set out for the Holy Land in 1096. This would later become known as the People's Crusade, which claimed its first victims in the Rhineland, where Jewish communities were massacred in one of medieval Europe's earliest outbreaks of antisemitism . A better-organized army of European upper nobility was eventually assembled in Constantinople between November 1096 and April 1097. Unprecedented bloodshed The Holy Land, located between what is today Turkey , Syria and Egypt , was a polyglot society divided among Sunni Seljuk Turkish warlords and the Shi'a Fatimid Caliphate. Godfrey of Bouillon, a Frankish knight, led the siege of Jerusalem in 1099 Image: Ken Welsh/UIG/IMAGO It took some time for locals to understand that this wasn't just another raid, said Mohamad El-Merheb, an expert on the premodern Islamic Eastern Mediterranean at SOAS University of London: "It takes maybe at least a decade for some people to see it as an ideological project to convert and take the Holy Land." "Some of the cities are well defended, some are not. But it is all in the context of very fragmented political power," El-Merheb said. The Crusaders had what El-Merheb describes as a series of swift conquests in important cities such as Edessa and Antioch. Despite these early victories, life fighting a Holy War was grueling. The majority returned home, or died of disease, hunger or sheer exhaustion. When they captured Jerusalem in 1099, Crusaders massacred thousands of Muslims and Jews because they couldn't tell them apart. The Crusades remain a fixture in the popular imagination through symbols, stories and films such as 'The Crusades' (1935), a historical drama directed by Cecil B. DeMille Image: Everett Collection/IMAGO Many historians consider the fall of the city of Acre to Mamluk warriors in 1291 to be the end of the Crusades in the Holy Land. Later crusades were also called, however, including to block the advance of Ottoman Turks in Eastern Europe in 14th century. "Reconquista" Christian military campaigns aimed to retake the Iberian Peninsula from Muslim rule into the late 15th century. The Crusades meet the culture wars The legacy of the Crusades remains a powerful and polarizing cultural touchstone. In both the East and the West, the historical memory of these medieval holy wars is frequently repurposed to frame modern identities, politics and conflicts. In 2001, US President George W. Bush caused uproar when he described the so-called "War on Terror" as a "crusade," a term already used by Osama bin Laden to frame US-led wars as religious wars intended to destroy Islam . Saladin, depicted here receiving the English Bishop of Salisbury in 1192, successfully united fractured Muslim territories from Egypt to Mesopotamia Image: GRANGER Historical Picture Archive/IMAGO In his propaganda to legitimize his global jihad, bin Laden also invoked the legacy of Saladin, a legendary Kurdish commander revered to this day as the hero who recaptured Jerusalem from the Crusaders in 1187. "As of the 19th century, Saladin specifically becomes a symbol of fighting Western colonialism and imperialism," said El-Merheb. "Throughout the 20th century, a lot of Islamist groups also start referring to the Western powers as Crusaders, so this becomes part of political nationalism on the state level and also on a more popular level in films, for example. This is happening in the West now in the opposite way." Crusader symbolism has long been used by far-right movements in the United States and Europe to promote narratives of civilizational conflict. The Latin phrase "deus vult," or "God wills it," has been used by figures including far-right mass murderer Anders Breivik and Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party, while France's far-right party Reconquête draws its name from the Reconquista campaigns. US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth famously has "deus vult" tattooed on his arm and a Crusader cross on his chest. In "American Crusade," Hegseth calls the Crusades a "defensive" and "existential" war to defend Europe against Islamic expansion Image: Sra Madelyn Keech/DoD/ZUMA/IMAGO But El-Merheb believes that such references often reduce the Crusades to a simple clash between Christianity and Islam, "which really was never simply the case." This framing, he said, ignores "how the Crusades were from the start very antisemitic projects, or violent projects against other Christian communities in Europe such as the Cathars in France, against Byzantium and the Islamic world and ignores the many cross-religious alliances between Muslims and Crusaders." Along the way, he said, these politicians are also forgetting how violent and destructive these historical campaigns were. https://telex.hu/kulfold/2026/10/23/dmit.text: Menü Kereső Ránk számíthattok! 3000 új támogatót keresünk Csatlakozom Putyin szóvivője szerint novemberben Abu-Dzabiban tervezik megtartani a háromoldalú tárgyalásokat Ukrajnáról Külföld frissítve Vida Benjámin Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Dmitrij Peszkov, az orosz elnök sajtótitkára újságírói kérdésre kijelentette, hogy november első felében, Abu-Dzabiban Oroszország, Ukrajna és az Egyesült Államok részvételével tervezik megtartani az ukrajnai rendezésről szóló tárgyalások újabb fordulóját. Megjegyezte, hogy semmilyen lehetőséget nem lehet kizárni, így az európaiak részvételét sem. „Előzetesen semmit sem lehet kizárni. Azok a tárgyalások azonban, amelyekről beszélünk, és amelyeket november első felére terveznek Abu-Dzabiban, háromoldalú formátumban zajlanak majd” – mondta Peszkov a TASZSZ orosz állami hírügynökség szerint, miután arról kérdezték, hogy a Kreml kizárja-e annak a lehetőségét, hogy a tárgyalásokon részt vegyen Európa. Peszkov az MTI szerint arról is beszélt, hogy Oroszország és Ukrajna biztonsága „a békés rendezés elérésének egyik rendkívül fontos alkotóeleme, amely nélkül átfogó megoldás nem lehetséges”. Putyin sajtótitkára szerint Brüsszel álláspontjától függ, hogy van-e értelme részt vennie az ukrajnai békefolyamatról szóló tárgyalásokon az Európai Unió különmegbízottjának. Volodimir Zelenszkij ukrán elnök pénteken megerősítette, hogy Ukrajna, Oroszország és az Egyesült Államok béketárgyalói megállapodtak abban, hogy november első felében Abu-Dzabiban technikai szintű egyeztetést tartanak. Hozzátette, reméli, hogy ezután a három ország vezetői is találkoznak majd egymással. Zelenszkij a Reuters szerint azt is elmondta, hogy pénteken egyeztetett az Egyesült Államok különmegbízottjaival, Jared Kushnerrel és Steve Witkoff-fal. Az ukrán elnök szerint minden békemegállapodásnak szilárd biztonsági garanciákat kell biztosítania Ukrajna számára, valamint tíz évre szóló finanszírozást is az ukrán hadsereg fenntartására. Zelenszkij azt mondta, elengedhetetlen, hogy a technikai egyeztetéseket a három ország vezetőinek találkozója kövesse. Vlagyimir Putyin orosz elnök szerdán beleegyezett abba, hogy újrakezdik a háromoldalú tárgyalásokat Washingtonnal és Kijevvel, erről egy Kreml-tisztviselő számolt be . A háromoldalú tárgyalások középpontjában „Oroszország és Ukrajna biztonsági rendszerének kiépítése lesz a konfliktus befejezése után” – fogalmazott a tisztviselő. Steve Witkoff, az Egyesült Államok különmegbízottja szerdán személyesen tárgyalt Vlagyimir Putyin orosz elnökkel Szentpéterváron. A tárgyalásról Witkoff azt is mondta az orosz elnöknek: „Annyit beszél arról, hogy az én elnököm, Trump elnök emberséges. Ön is emberséges, uram, és ezt nagyra értékelem, dicséretet érdemel, és még egyszer köszönöm.” Ezt annak az amerikai állampolgárnak a szabadon engedése miatt mondhatta, aki évek óta orosz fogságban volt. Witkoff kedden Oslóban tárgyalt Volodimir Zelenszkij ukrán elnökkel, Finnország és Norvégia vezetőivel, valamint európai és NATO-képviselőkkel. Az amerikai források szerint a norvégiai találkozó konstruktívan zajlott . Donald Trump amerikai elnök nemrég közölte, hogy nyitott lenne egy háromoldalú találkozóra Hszi Csin-ping kínai és Vlagyimir Putyin orosz elnökkel, a megbeszélések pedig a nukleáris leszerelésre összpontosíthatnának. Dmitrij Peszkov a lehetséges találkozót fontosnak minősítette, de hozzátette, hogy ez nem lesz azonos fajsúlyú a II. világháború idején a későbbi világrendet meghatározó találkozóval. Peszkov szerint az orosz alapállás az, „hogy senki ne kényszerítsen senkire semmiféle világrendet”. Cikkünk frissült Volodimir Zelenszkij nyilatkozatával. https://marketbusinessnews.com/eu-touris.text: Business News EU tourist accommodation records 3.14 billion nights in 2025 Written by Christian Nordqvist Published: 15:20, October 16, 2026 Tourist accommodation across the European Union recorded 3.14 billion guest nights in 2025, up 4.1% from the previous year, according to annual figures released by Eurostat on October 16. The increase amounted to about 123 million additional nights. Holiday and other short-stay accommodation expanded faster than hotels, giving businesses a more detailed picture of where demand grew. The figures cover stays in hotels and similar establishments, holiday accommodation and campsites. They measure overnight stays rather than the number of individual travelers or the money they spent. Short stays outpace hotels Eurostat’s annual accommodation report shows that nights in holiday and other short-stay accommodation rose 9.2%. Campsites recorded a 5.8% increase, while hotels and similar establishments grew 1.7%. Hotels remained the largest category, accounting for 61.4% of nights. Holiday and other short-stay accommodation represented 24.8%, with camping making up the remaining 13.8%. The category differences matter to operators and suppliers. An increase concentrated in apartments, holiday properties or campsites may create different demand for cleaning, booking systems and equipment than an equivalent increase in hotel stays. The short-stay category should not be treated as a count of bookings through particular online platforms. It is an accommodation classification. Most demand comes from within Europe In its October 16 release , Eurostat said domestic visitors and guests from other EU countries accounted for 80.9% of all nights. Visitors from other European countries contributed another 10.4%. Guests from the Americas accounted for 4.9%, compared with 2.6% from Asia. Nights by visitors from Asia increased 15.4%, although that growth started from a much smaller base than European demand. For accommodation businesses, this suggests that a strong overseas growth rate needs to be considered alongside the size of the customer group. Nearby and domestic markets still supplied most of the recorded overnight business. Across the EU, tourism intensity reached seven accommodation nights per resident, compared with 6.7 in 2024. Croatia, Malta and Cyprus recorded the highest ratios. The measure compares visitor activity with the resident population; it does not directly measure profitability or pressure at a particular destination. More nights do not necessarily mean higher margins The figures complement MBN’s recent reporting on EU residents’ spending on foreign and domestic trips . That dataset follows residents’ travel expenditure, while the new release measures nights in accommodation located within the EU. Neither rising nights nor higher spending alone establishes that operators earned better margins. Room prices, staffing costs, occupancy patterns and the mix of properties also affect commercial performance. There is a comparability qualification too. Eurostat says changes in coverage in Italy and Lithuania affected the 2025 statistics, so some reported growth reflects improved measurement. Business plans should therefore use local and accommodation-specific figures alongside the EU headline. Christian Nordqvist Christian has a love for the English Language. He spent various years as an English Language Teacher and then became an accomplished writer. He has had 80 books published, including “English for the Pharmaceutical Industry”, “English for Shipping” and “English for Law”. Prior to creating Market Business News, Christian co-founded Medical News Today and was Editor-in-Chief for the website for several years.
